denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 19318 (bilateral reduction mammaplasty) with date of service 2026-07-03. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation submitted does not establish failure of conservative therapy or an expected resection weight meeting the policy threshold.

criteria.text: Symptoms attributable to macromastia documented for at least 6 months, such as neck, shoulder, or upper back pain, shoulder grooving, or inframammary intertrigo.
At least 3 months of conservative treatment, including a supportive garment plus physical therapy, analgesics, or dermatologic treatment of intertrigo, without adequate relief.
Estimated resection weight per breast at or above the 22nd percentile of the Schnur sliding scale for the patient's body surface area.
Photographic documentation of macromastia and shoulder grooving.

chart.text: Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 16 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.

50 year old woman here about her breasts, referred by her primary. Exam: large pendulous breasts, nipple to notch 36 on the right and 37 on the left, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both inframammary folds. Discussed reduction, risks, scars, sensation, the works. Her history otherwise: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, prediabetes, diet controlled, reflux on omeprazole as needed. Surgeries: wisdom teeth. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works as a nurse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. She has had the neck and upper back pain for 10 months now, maybe longer, says it is daily by the afternoon. The bra straps have worn grooves into both shoulders and she gets the rash under the breasts every summer. We talked about PT and I gave her the referral and told her to get a properly fitted bra. She has not tried anything yet. She is 5 foot 4, 150 pounds, which puts BSA right around 1.75. Schnur 22nd percentile at that BSA is about 407 grams. I am estimating 560 grams on the right and 539 on the left.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Back to go over the plan. Symptoms unchanged. We went through the operation again and she wants to proceed if insurance will cover it. Vitals today 140 over 87, pulse 64. Has not started PT, says the copay is a problem. Did buy a new bra, not sure it is the right size. Still symptomatic.
Standard pre-op photo series taken today, front, both obliques, both laterals. Grooving visible at both shoulders in the AP view, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both folds.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.6, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Vitamin D came back 16. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Blood pressure check. 141 over 92 today, 134 over 82 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 217, LDL 113, HDL 58, triglycerides 168. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Pre-op visit. Consent signed, marked the plan on her in the mirror, superomedial pedicle, Wise pattern. Labs fine. Stop the ibuprofen a week out.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-2 (conservative) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan or a shortfall, not completed treatment or a met threshold.
